name: Schur's numbers (version 2).
comment: Largest number such that there is an n-coloring of the integers 1, ..., a(n) such that each color is sum-free, that is, no color contains a triple x + y = z. - _Charles R Greathouse IV_, Jun 11 2013
The best known lower bounds for the next terms are due to Fredricksen and Sweet (see links): a(6) >= 536 and a(7) >= 1680. - _Dmitry Kamenetsky_, Oct 23 2019
A partition showing that a(7) >= 1696 was demonstrated in 2021, along with some recurrence relationships for lower bounds on a(n). - _Fred Rowley_, Mar 01 2023
Chen-Zhu-Long refines lower bound estimates as follows: a(6) >= 537, a(8) >= 5372, a(11) >= 204208, and a(13) >= 2042082. - _Michael De Vlieger_, Oct 23 2026
reference: R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, E11 and E12.
link: Zhiyang Chen, Ligeng Zhu, and Fan Long, A new lower bound for the sixth Schur number: S(6) >= 537, arXiv:2610.31362 [math.CO], 2026.

Harold Fredricksen and Melvin M. Sweet, Symmetric Sum-Free Partitions and Lower Bounds for Schur Number, Electron. J. Combin. 7 (2000), Art. R32.
Solomon W. Golomb and Leonard D. Baumert, Backtrack Programming, J. ACM 12(4) (1965), 516-524. [Reference corrected by _N. J. A. Sloane_, May 18 2020]

Marijn J. H. Heule, Schur Number Five, AAAI 2018.
